description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy across three different measures—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—across a range of initial confidence values from 0.86 to 1.00. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," is scaled linearly with a range from 0.86 to 1.00, marked at intervals of 0.02. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, with a linear scale and marked at intervals of 0.2. The blue line, representing Final Accuracy, begins at approximately 0.93 when the initial confidence is 0.86 and remains relatively stable, fluctuating slightly around 0.95 to 0.98, before ending at about 0.97 when the initial confidence reaches 1.00. The green line, representing Initial Accuracy, starts at around 0.65 and shows a general upward trend, increasing to approximately 0.92 by the end of the range. The orange line, representing Δ Accuracy, begins at about 0.28 and decreases to a low of approximately 0.02 near an initial confidence of 0.95, then rises slightly to about 0.21 at the end of the range. Error bars are present for each data point, indicating variability in the measurements.
